question: According to current WHO/FIGO definitions, PRIMARY postpartum haemorrhage is defined as blood loss of:

answers.text: ≥250 mL following any mode of delivery within 24 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. 250 mL is below the accepted threshold; this would not constitute a PPH by any standard definition.

answers.text: ≥500 mL following vaginal delivery OR ≥1000 mL following caesarean section within 24 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Primary PPH is defined as ≥500 mL after vaginal delivery or ≥1000 mL after caesarean section (or any blood loss causing haemodynamic compromise) within 24 hours of delivery.

answers.text: ≥750 mL following vaginal delivery OR ≥1500 mL following caesarean section within 24 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. These thresholds are too high; waiting for 750 mL / 1500 mL before acting would represent dangerous under-recognition of PPH.

answers.text: Any visible bleeding persisting more than 30 minutes after placental delivery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. PPH is defined by volume (and haemodynamic effect), not by duration of bleeding alone.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the WHO/FIGO PPH definitions. The thresholds differ by mode of delivery: ≥500 mL for vaginal and ≥1000 mL for caesarean delivery.
Well done. Primary PPH = ≥500 mL (vaginal) or ≥1000 mL (caesarean) within 24 hours; severe PPH = ≥1000 mL with haemodynamic compromise.
